name: Apple Xcode Cloud

modes.label: Xcode Cloud compute hours (Xcode build/test only)

sizes.name: Xcode Cloud compute hour (Apple-managed, spec not published)

modes.note: Hour price = marginal rate of the 250 h / 1,000 h / 10,000 h subscriptions ($99.99/250, $399.99/1,000, $3,999.99/10,000 = ~$0.40/h). Hour packs are encoded as plans with included_usd = hours x $0.40. A compute hour is summed task time ("running 5 tests of 12 minutes each equals one compute hour").

plans.name: Included with Apple Developer Program (25 h/month)
plans.note: Requires Apple Developer Program membership ($99/yr). 25 compute hours/month; unused hours don't roll over; no overage - builds beyond the quota need a paid subscription.

caveats: Xcode build/test workflows only: Xcode Cloud runs Xcode actions (build, test, analyze, archive) for Apple-platform apps. Shell runs only as the three custom build-script hooks (ci_post_clone.sh, ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh, ci_post_xcodebuild.sh) inside a workflow, without sudo ("You can't obtain administrator privileges by using sudo"), and files they create are deleted. No SSH, no interactive shell, no GUI/desktop automation: not usable as an agent sandbox or macOS desktop.
Subscriptions are fixed hour packs with no published overage; beyond the pack you must upgrade. included_usd at $0.40/h approximates that; the 100 h pack is really $0.50/h.
Billing granularity not published (granularity_s null); ephemeral build environments are destroyed after each build.
Apple Developer Program membership required (its fee not modelled).

Upgrading a subscription starts a new billing period immediately and resets the quota to 0 (new plan's hours replace, not add to, the remainder); downgrades take effect next period; cancel -> back to 25 h.
Subscriptions are priced in USD or in local currency where available (local prices shown only in the Apple Developer app; localized web pages jp/cn list the same US$ prices).
Hidden infrastructure-validation builds may run duplicate builds/custom scripts (opt-out in App Store Connect); Apple says they don't consume your build minutes.

fleet.verification: Apple Developer Program membership; Account Holder manages subscriptions.
fleet.tiers: Subscriptions purchase monthly compute hours (25 included, higher paid tiers); not a published concurrent-build fleet allocation.
fleet.notes: No universal new-account concurrent build/VM quota or increase-review SLA found. Parallel build/test operations consume hours; simulator count and build hours must not be equated to machine concurrency.
